transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: Mon Jul 21 2025 | 15:00 PT - 16:00 PT (approx)
Duration: 52 minutes logged
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luca (Redwood SE), Hannah (Redwood CSM), Samir (Meridian Head of ML), Aisha (Platform Eng), Daniel (Security)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time today. We wanted to do a quick alignment — Samir, you mentioned a subscription uplift and EU onramp in your note, want to confirm scope?
[00:12] Samir: Yeah, hi Maya. Quick context — we're hitting higher token volumes in our production chat assistant and finance vertical. Leadership has approved a bump, roughly 30% more committed units, and they also want data to be resident in the EU for a new customer cohort. So two things: capacity ramp and EU onramp.
[00:30] Aisha: And a related ask from infra is basically — we need to see a Private or Dedicated plan that meets our VPC/KMS rules. We're not ready to go fully on-prem but want a pilot on Private in our Azure tenancy.
[00:45] Luca: Got it. From a technical POV we can outline two paths: Dedicated reserved capacity in our managed infra (predictable throughput) or Redwood Private deployed into your VPC with customer-managed keys. Tradeoffs are predictable latency and simpler provisioning for Dedicated vs data residency and control for Private.
[01:05] Daniel: Quick security note — procurement will require SOC2 + evidence of KMS/HSM use, RBAC audit logs, SAML SSO, and an option for audit logs retention within EU. Can you confirm those are available?
[01:18] Hannah: Yes — we have SOC2 Type II, we can share the report. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via KMS integration; audit logs are available and can be routed to your SIEM. There's an RBAC model and SSO via SAML/Okta. We'll surface the doc pack after this call.
[01:35] Samir: Great. On the capacity side — latency is critical for a real-time assistant, 95th percentile under 220ms is the ask. Cost can flex a bit but we still need visibility into per-token unit economics for the uplift.
[01:50] Luca: Right. A few technical details to unpack: average sequence lengths, KV cache hit rates, and batching behavior will drive cost. Our Optimize tooling recommends quantization profiles and batching thresholds by workload; for real-time we often avoid large batch windows. We can run a small benchmark with your sample model and traffic pattern to get concrete numbers.
[02:10] Aisha: The benchmark — what would we need to provide? We have a distilled variant of our model (6B) and an obfuscated prompt set. We can provide synthetic traces.
[02:22] Luca: Perfect. We need: sample model artifact (or model name), representative request traces (timestamps, input lengths), and target SLOs. We'll spin up a dedicated benchmark harness — can do both Dedicated and Private variants so you can compare latency and cost.
[02:35] Maya: On contract terms, you're looking for a 12-month renewal with an uplift and optional top-up credits for burst. Any constraints on billing or commitment structure?
[02:45] Samir: Prefer single annual invoice if possible. Also would like a clause that allows a 10% downward adjustment if usage falls below 85% of committed units after quarter one.
[02:55] Hannah: We can work with finance on that. I'll loop in legal to draft language, but we usually have a consumption reconciliation clause — we'll surface an example contract.
[03:05] Daniel: For EU data residency — if we go Private, can logs and KV cache stay in customer-controlled subnets? We can't have any token metadata egressing outside the EU.
[03:18] Luca: In Private deployment we run a customer-controlled control plane and data plane optionally in your tenancy; KV cache and ephemeral state will be within the region. For Hosted/Dedicated variants, we have region routing and a strict data policy but some metadata may be stored in US by default — so for your requirement Private is the most straightforward.
[03:38] Samir: Ok that aligns. What about SLA and fallback? If Private pilot doesn't meet perf, do we have a fallback to Dedicated in EU?
[03:48] Maya: Yes — we can craft a fallback policy in the rollout plan. The platform supports smart routing and automatic fallback to a compatible variant if capacity is constrained — that's built into our deployment abstraction. We'll document the canary and failover steps.
[04:05] Aisha: On the uplift numbers, can you share the line-item cost delta for quantized vs fp16 models? Our finance wants ballpark numbers to approve the uplift.
[04:15] Luca: We'll produce a cost delta sheet — quantized can reduce per-token costs significantly but may add a small quality delta. We'll include recommendations from Redwood Optimize: suggested quant levels for 6B model families and expected throughput improvements.
[04:30] Maya: Alright let's confirm action items — Luca will run the benchmark once we get artifacts, Hannah will send SOC2 and security pack, Maya will send pricing worksheet and proposed contract language. Proposed benchmark date Aug 4, does that work for Meridian?
[04:45] Samir: Aug 4 is doable, we'll target to provide artifacts by July 28.
[04:52] Daniel: Also flagging — procurement needs to see competitor comparison notes; specifically they will ask why not Vertex AI or Anthropic. Maybe a short doc is helpful.
[05:02] Maya: We can provide a short comparator that focuses on control plane differences, unit economics, and observability.
[05:12] Aisha: One last nit — network egress costs. If Private is in our tenancy, egress is internal, but for Dedicated what are typical cross-region egress implications?
[05:25] Luca: For Dedicated, traffic within the region is kept local; cross-region fallbacks can incur egress. We'll include a note in the pricing sheet about egress assumptions.
[05:38] Samir: Sounds good. If we get the numbers and the security pack, we can sign off at director level and push to finance.
[05:46] Maya: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items we discussed and confirm the benchmark slot.

Recap (end):
- Meridian to provide model artifact and trace by 2025-07-28.
- Redwood to share pricing worksheet, SOC2/security pack, benchmark playbook.
- Proposed benchmark window Aug 4; Luca to run Dedicated and Private comparisons.

End of meeting.
